questions.q: Nitrobenzene is reduced with zinc dust and aqueous NH₄Cl. The product is:
questions.explain: In the nearly neutral NH₄Cl medium the reduction stops after four electrons at C₆H₅NHOH.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene is treated with LiAlH₄ followed by H₃O⁺. The product is:
questions.explain: Metal hydrides couple two aryl nitrogens to give C₆H₅–N=N–C₆H₅; the trap is aniline, which LiAlH₄ gives only from aliphatic nitro compounds.

questions.q: Match the reagent with the product of nitrobenzene reduction. Which pair is INCORRECT?
questions.explain: Zn/NaOH is an alkaline reduction and gives the bimolecular product azobenzene; phenylhydroxylamine comes from neutral Zn/NH₄Cl.

questions.q: Why is Fe/HCl preferred over Sn/HCl for the large-scale preparation of aniline?
options: Iron reduces only one nitro group of a dinitro compound
FeCl₂ formed is hydrolysed and regenerates HCl, so only a little acid is needed
Iron gives free aniline directly without any base
Iron reduction stops at the hydroxylamine stage
questions.explain: Regeneration of HCl by hydrolysis of FeCl₂ makes the iron process cheaper. Fe/HCl still reduces every nitro group and still gives the anilinium salt, which needs NaOH.
